date.label: Undated 1 Chronicles narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Reuben was the firstborn of Israel, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the chief ruler; but the birthright was Joseph's.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. The younger-son pattern is the Bible Odyssey article's subject, read in full in this dossier.

claims.claim: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel were Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: A single line runs from Joel through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaia, and Baal to Beerah, "whom Tilgathpilneser king of Assyria carried away captive: he was prince of the Reubenites."
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. The Assyria article (lines 147–148) cites 1 Chr 5:6 with 5:26 for Tiglath-pileser's deportation of Gilead.

claims.claim: The brethren by their families, when the genealogy was reckoned, were headed by Jeiel and Zechariah; Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel, dwelt in Aroer, even unto Nebo and Baalmeon.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: Bela's line inhabited eastward unto the entering in of the wilderness from the river Euphrates, because their cattle were multiplied in the land of Gilead; and in the days of Saul they made war with the Hagarites, who fell by their hand, and they dwelt in their tents throughout all the east land of Gilead.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Hagrites"; "throughout all the land east of Gilead").

claims.claim: The children of Gad dwelt over against them, in the land of Bashan unto Salcah. Joel was the chief, and Shapham the next, and Jaanai, and Shaphat in Bashan; and their brethren of the house of their fathers were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Heber, seven.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Jacan" and "Eber"). "Salcah" is the stored spelling; the BibleHub/BLB KJV text reads "Salchah" (Class B edition variant, KJV verification report).

claims.claim: A second Gadite line runs through Abihail the son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz, to Ahi the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, chief of the house of their fathers. They dwelt in Gilead in Bashan, and in her towns, and in all the suburbs of Sharon, upon their borders.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Jehishai" for "Jeshishai"; "the open lands of the plain" for "the suburbs of Sharon"). The Sharon identification is unresolved (see §8).

claims.claim: All these were reckoned by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. The identification of the Jeroboam as Jeroboam II is probable, not stated by the text (see §8).

claims.claim: The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful in war, were four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore, that went out to the war.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "forty and four thousand seven hundred and threescore, that were able to go forth to war"). The figure is carried as the text's muster figure (see §8).

claims.claim: They made war with the Hagarites, with Jetur, and Nephish, and Nodab; and they were helped against them, and the Hagarites were delivered into their hand, and all that were with them: "for they cried to God in the battle, and he was intreated of them; because they put their trust in him." They took fifty thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand asses, and an hundred thousand men; "for there fell down many slain, because the war was of God. And they dwelt in their steads until the captivity."
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Naphish" for "Nephish"; "souls of men a hundred thousand").

claims.claim: The children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land, increasing from Bashan unto Baal-hermon and Senir, and unto mount Hermon. Their heads were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valour, famous men, and heads of the house of their fathers.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Baal-hermon and Senir and mount Hermon, where they increased").

claims.claim: They transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them. And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgathpilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river Gozan, unto this day. Pul and Tilgathpilneser are one king, Tiglath-pileser III, who reigned in Babylon under the name Pulu.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Tillegath-pilneser"; "broke faith with the God of their fathers, and went astray after the gods of the peoples of the land"). BiblicalTraining, "Assyria," lines 127–134, 147–148: the two names are one king, confirmed by a Babylonian king list; his 734–732 BC campaigns stripped Gilead and deported its people.

claims.claim: The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari; and the sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel. (MT 5:27–28; see the seam note in §3.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: The children of Amram were Aaron, and Moses, and Miriam. The sons also of Aaron were Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. (MT 5:29.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: The line runs Eleazar, Phinehas, Abishua, Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, Ahimaaz, Azariah, Johanan, Azariah — "he it is that executed the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem" — Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, Shallum, Hilkiah, Azariah, Seraiah, and Jehozadak, who "went into captivity, when the LORD carried away Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar." (MT 5:30–41.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "he it is that executed the priest's office in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem"). BiblicalTraining, "Solomon's Temple," lines 2–8, 14–19: the temple was the permanent sanctuary Solomon built, replacing the tabernacle; David gathered the materials and organised the service.

claims.claim: The list begins a second time: "The sons of Levi; Gershom, Kohath, and Merari." The sons of Gershom were Libni and Shimei; the sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel; the sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. "And these are the families of the Levites according to their fathers." (MT 6:1–4.) Gershom here is the Gershon of 6:1 under a variant spelling.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (MT 6:1 reads Gershom where MT 5:27 reads Gershon).

claims.claim: Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son, Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeaterai his son. (MT 6:5–6.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Jeatherai" for "Jeaterai").

claims.claim: The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son, Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son, Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son. (MT 6:7–9.) The name Amminadab in this position, where 6:2 names Izhar, is unresolved (see §8).
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: The sons of Elkanah were Amasai and Ahimoth; and as for Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah were Zophai his son, and Nahath his son, Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son. And the sons of Samuel were "the firstborn Vashni, and Abiah." (MT 6:10–13.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "the first-born Vashni; then Abiah"). The Vashni reading itself is treated in 1CCL-02-020.

claims.claim: The stored text names Samuel's firstborn "Vashni," while 1 Samuel names Samuel's eldest son Joel and his second son Abiah, and this same chapter traces Heman back through "Joel, the son of Shemuel" (6:33). The Hebrew form behind "Vashni" is very close to the ordinary expression for "and the second," and most interpreters conclude a copyist dropped Joel's name, leaving the phrase to be read later as a proper name; some Greek manuscripts of the Septuagint and the Syriac preserve the fuller reading with Joel. On this reading there was no son of Samuel named Vashni.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. BiblicalTraining, "Vashni," read in full (15 lines). BiblicalTraining, "Samuel," lines 111–116: Samuel appointed his sons Joel and Abijah as judges at Beersheba.

claims.claim: The sons of Merari were Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzza his son, Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son. (MT 6:14–15.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Uzzah" for "Uzza").

claims.claim: These are they whom David set over the service of song in the house of the LORD, after that the ark had rest. They ministered before the dwelling place of the tabernacle of the congregation with singing, until Solomon had built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem: "and then they waited on their office according to their order." (MT 6:16–17.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "they took their station at their service according to their order"). BiblicalTraining, "Solomon's Temple," lines 34–39: David organised the Levites, priests, musicians, and gatekeepers for their future service.

claims.claim: Heman a singer, of the sons of the Kohathites, is traced from Joel, the son of Shemuel, through Elkanah, Jeroham, Eliel, Toah, Zuph, Elkanah, Mahath, Amasai, Elkanah, Joel, Azariah, Zephaniah, Tahath, Assir, Ebiasaph, Korah, Izhar, and Kohath, to Levi, the son of Israel. (MT 6:18–23.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. BiblicalTraining, "Samuel," lines 24–27: Chronicles names Samuel's grandson Heman, one of the chief musicians David appointed.

claims.claim: His brother Asaph, who stood on his right hand, is traced from Berachiah through Shimea, Michael, Baaseiah, Malchiah, Ethni, Zerah, Adaiah, Ethan, Zimmah, Shimei, Jahath, and Gershom, to Levi. (MT 6:24–28.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: Their brethren the sons of Merari stood on the left hand: Ethan the son of Kishi, traced through Abdi, Malluch, Hashabiah, Amaziah, Hilkiah, Amzi, Bani, Shamer, Mahli, and Mushi, to Merari, the son of Levi. (MT 6:29–32.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. 1 Chr 15:17 names the same singer Ethan "the son of Kushaiah"; the two forms are carried as given.

claims.claim: Their brethren also the Levites were appointed unto all manner of service of the tabernacle of the house of God. (MT 6:33.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre. BiblicalTraining, "Book of Numbers," lines 85–91: the Levites are counted separately because they served the sanctuary; Kohath, Gershon, and Merari carry its parts.

claims.claim: Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, and were appointed for all the work of the place most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded. (MT 6:34.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son, Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son, Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son, Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son. (MT 6:35–38.) This short line duplicates 6:4–8 and ends at Zadok and Ahimaaz, where the long line runs on to Jehozadak and the captivity.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: These are their dwelling places throughout their castles in their coasts, of the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites: "for theirs was the lot." They gave them Hebron in the land of Judah, and the suburbs thereof round about it. "But the fields of the city, and the villages thereof, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh." (MT 6:39–41.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "for theirs was the [first] lot").

claims.claim: To the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of Judah, namely, Hebron, the city of refuge, and Libnah with her suburbs, and Jattir, and Eshtemoa, with their suburbs, and Hilen with her suburbs, Debir with her suburbs, and Ashan with her suburbs, and Bethshemesh with her suburbs; and out of Benjamin, Geba with her suburbs, and Alemeth with her suburbs, and Anathoth with her suburbs. "All their cities throughout their families were thirteen cities." (MT 6:42–45.) Eleven cities are named while the total is stated as thirteen (see §5).
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "the city of refuge, Hebron; Libnah also").

claims.claim: Unto the sons of Kohath, which were left of the family of that tribe, were cities given out of the half tribe, namely, out of the half tribe of Manasseh, by lot, ten cities. (MT 6:46.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: To the sons of Gershom throughout their families, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities. (MT 6:47.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: Unto the sons of Merari were given by lot, throughout their families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities. (MT 6:48.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: The children of Israel gave to the Levites these cities with their suburbs; and they gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities, which are called by their names. The residue of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their coasts out of the tribe of Ephraim. (MT 6:49–51.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: They gave unto them, of the cities of refuge, Shechem in mount Ephraim with her suburbs; also Gezer, Jokmeam, Bethhoron, Aijalon, and Gathrimmon; and out of the half tribe of Manasseh, Aner with her suburbs, and Bileam with her suburbs, for the family of the remnant of the sons of Kohath. (MT 6:52–55.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre.

claims.claim: Unto the sons of Gershom were given, out of the half tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with her suburbs, and Ashtaroth with her suburbs; and out of Issachar, Kedesh, Daberath, Ramoth, and Anem; and out of Asher, Mashal, Abdon, Hukok, and Rehob; and out of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kirjathaim. (MT 6:56–61.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Dobrath" for "Daberath").

claims.claim: Unto the rest of the children of Merari were given, out of Zebulun, Rimmon with her suburbs, Tabor with her suburbs; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho, on the east side of Jordan, out of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness with her suburbs, and Jahzah with her suburbs, Kedemoth also with her suburbs, and Mephaath with her suburbs; and out of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbs, and Mahanaim with her suburbs, and Heshbon with her suburbs, and Jazer with her suburbs. (MT 6:62–66.)
claims.evidence: Stored KJV read in full; Hebrew + JPS 1917 read in full, Mechon Mamre (JPS: "Rimmono" for "Rimmon"; "Jahaz" for "Jahzah"). BiblicalTraining, "Ramoth-gilead," lines 18–25: Ramoth in Gilead was a city of refuge for the Gadites and a Merarite Levitical town. BiblicalTraining, "Heshbon," lines 40–44: Heshbon stood on the boundary between Reuben and Gad and appears among the towns from Gad given to Merari.

connections.note: Jacob speaks over Reuben his firstborn: pre-eminent in dignity and power, yet unstable as water, he will not excel, because he went up to his father's bed. The father's sentence is the reason the Chronicler gives for the birthright passing to Joseph's sons.

The sons of Ishmael are listed by name, among them Jetur and Naphish. The Hagarites whom the eastern tribes fought, with Jetur and Nephish beside them, were most likely desert peoples of Ishmael's line, on the fringe east of Gilead where the herdsmen's ranges ran.

In the list of those who went down into Egypt with Jacob, the sons of Levi are named as Gershon, Kohath, and Merari — the same three heads under whom the Chronicler orders the whole tribe two books later.

The sons of Levi are listed again at the exodus: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, with Kohath's sons Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, and Amram's children Aaron and Moses. Targets 6:16–19 and 6:20–22. The Chronicler's Levi list is the same family, carried forward to the exile.

Nadab and Abihu, the two eldest sons of Aaron, offer strange fire before the LORD and die there. They are named in the Chronicler's line at 6:3 and then never again; the priesthood runs through their younger brother Eleazar.

The children of Reuben and of Gad, seeing that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead is a place for cattle, and having a very great multitude of cattle, ask Moses to give them the land for a possession and not to bring them over Jordan. The request is the beginning of the eastern settlement.

Moses gives to the children of Gad, to the children of Reuben, and to half the tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon and the kingdom of Og, with their cities and lands. Targets 32:33–34 and 32:39–42. The threefold grant is the settlement the Chronicler's chapter 5 presupposes.

On the plains of Moab the LORD commands Moses to give the Levites cities to dwell in, with suburbs for their cattle, from the inheritance of the other tribes — forty-eight cities in all. The command is the law behind the Chronicler's list of cities by lot.

Before Israel crosses the Jordan, Moses separates three cities on the east side for refuge: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. All three appear again as Levitical cities in the Chronicler's list.

At that time the LORD separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark, to stand before him, and to bless in his name; therefore Levi has no part nor inheritance with his brethren, for the LORD is his inheritance. The sentence explains why Levi's portion in the Chronicler's account is cities, not land.

The law of the firstborn gives the eldest son a double portion of all that his father has, and forbids a father to make the son of the beloved wife the firstborn instead. The law states the rule the Chronicler's opening verses show being set aside for Reuben.

With the tribe of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, Moses gave their inheritance beyond Jordan eastward, from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon through Gilead and Bashan to Mount Hermon. Targets 13:15–17, 13:24–28, and 13:29–31. The allotment is the map the Chronicler's settlements follow.

Joshua confirms the six cities of refuge: Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem in Mount Ephraim, and Hebron in the hill country of Judah west of the Jordan, with Bezer, Ramoth in Gilead, and Golan in Bashan on the east. All six are named again among the Chronicler's Levitical cities.

The heads of the Levites come to Eleazar and Joshua at Shiloh, and the cities are given by lot: thirteen to Aaron's sons, ten to the remaining Kohathites, thirteen to Gershom, twelve to Merari, forty-eight in all with their suburbs. Targets 21:4–8 and 21:13–40. The Chronicler's list is the same allotment, with the differences of detail the two lists show.

When Samuel is old he makes his sons judges over Israel at Beersheba: the name of his firstborn is Joel, and the name of his second Abiah. They walk not in his ways, but turn aside after lucre, take bribes, and pervert judgment — and the elders ask for a king. The two names are the ones the Chronicler's verse renders differently.

The sons of Israel are listed: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Reuben stands first in the list and first in the book's order, though the genealogy that follows is not reckoned after the birthright.

David speaks to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brethren to be singers with instruments of music, and the Levites appoint Heman the son of Joel, Asaph the son of Berechiah, and Ethan the son of Kushaiah. Targets 15:17 and 15:19. The appointment is the act the Chronicler's chapter 6 records as the setting of the singers over the service of song.

Pul king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver; and in the days of Pekah, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carries them captive to Assyria. Targets 15:19–20 and 15:29. The two names are one king, and the taking of Gilead is the deportation the Chronicler dates to the same reign.

In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria takes Samaria and carries Israel away into Assyria, placing them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes. The destination is the same Halah, Habor, and Gozan to which the eastern tribes had been carried a decade earlier.

Dathan and Abiram, who strove against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah, are swallowed by the earth with their households — but the children of Korah died not. The Korah of the Chronicler's Kohath line is the rebel whose sons lived, and whose line runs on through the singers.
